title: Creative Newtech Ltd - 544631 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Creative Newtech FY26 consolidated total income rose 50.85% to INR2,717.51 crores, with PAT of INR70.29 crores, while Q4 receivables built up to about 20% of turnover.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR2,717.51 crores (up 50.85%), EBITDA of INR104 crores (up 41.7%, margin 3.83%) and PAT of INR70.29 crores (up 32.35%, margin 2.59%). Q4 FY26 total income was INR740.44 crores with EBITDA of INR29.39 crores and PAT of INR17.79 crores. Brand business (Honeywell, CyberPower and audio/air purifier lines) reached INR369.61 crores, 14.1% of revenue, against guidance of INR350-360 crores. Management flagged the Middle East war and container freight costs (Red Sea route cost up from about $1,500-1,700 to $7,500-8,000 per container) as headwinds to Middle East brand sales, and memory, storage and CPU costs up 30-40%.

financial_highlights.value: About INR171 crores at around 8-9% interest

segments.name: Market entry business
segments.commentary: About 85.9% of FY26 revenue (derived from brand share of 14.1%). Covers surveillance, AI, IoT, cybersecurity, drones, data center and HPC partnerships with Sparsh, Matrix, Dahua, Kaspersky and PDRL, plus EIZO displays.

segments.name: Brand business (Honeywell, CyberPower, audio, air purifiers)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR369.61 crores, ahead of INR359-360 crores guidance; audio outperformed. Management aspires to 50-60% annual brand growth and says Honeywell itself should grow at least 40-50%. Honeywell licence renews March 2027.

segments.name: Own brand (Vertual, launched May 2026)
segments.commentary: New in-house brand with air purifier and similar Honeywell categories, to launch first online in the US (Amazon warehouses already stocked) and in India, with material available from 22-23 May 2026. Management guided INR10-12 crores initial marketing spend and about 8-9 months to gain footing.

guidance_outlook: Internal target of at least 25-30% annual revenue growth and 30% absolute profit growth over the next 5-6 years; management says growth rate is ambitious but achievable for about 3-4 years.
Brand business targeted to grow 50-60% a year; Honeywell alone at least 40-50%; Honeywell brand expected to grow about 50% in FY27.
Brand business EBITDA expected at about 13% now, aiming for 17-18% at INR1,000 crore scale; long-run EBIT target 18-19% above INR1,000 crores.
Vision of a 50:50 market entry to brand split by 2030; aspiration to reach 3-4 brands near term and 6-7 long term, with 2-3 brands above INR1,000 crores.
Plan to separate brand and market entry businesses in 2-3 years, with a demerger process that could start after about 15 months; no plan in the next 15 months.
Middle East brand sales could fall to about 50% of current levels if shipments stay disrupted; management says price hikes and consumer sentiment may hit margins in FY27.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets rose to INR406 crores on ERP migration (Microsoft Business Central) with CRM and supply chain modules, new servers and software licences.
New distribution centre opened in Noida; new offices and set-up teams in Delhi and other locations for new businesses.
Working capital expected to be funded through debt and internal accruals for the next 15 months; equity raise only for an acquisition of about 30% of company size or a brand purchase.
Management is actively looking to acquire a surveillance/AI brand with a legacy, team and sales; expects a small acquired business (INR5 crore) could scale to INR10 crores in a year.
Brand business inventory: company holds 30-40 days of inventory to secure supply and hedge price increases; partners hold 45-60 days stock in Middle East.
demand_pricing: Management says price escalation is possible but demand should hold for 3-4 years, supported by India demographics, government push on AI, digital infrastructure and Make-in-India.

Higher Q4 gross and EBITDA margins attributed to Make-in-India surveillance and AI customers (PSU or government end-users) served via smaller vendors; management expects this margin mix to flow to the bottom line over time.
Raw material costs for memory, storage and CPUs up 30-40%; management says costs are being passed on but customers are beginning to feel the pressure and consumption may fall.

Brand categories: audio market about INR25,000 crores (India and abroad), air purifiers about INR3,000 crores in India, data-centre cables about INR4,000 crores in India; US air purifier market about INR28,000 crores, with about INR8,000 crores sold on Amazon.

Honeywell air purifier and accessories ambition is to be number 1 or 2 in India; air purifier currently close to number 2. Quick commerce grew over 100% across India, UAE and Saudi Arabia; 1 product sold every 60 seconds online in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Would demerging the higher-return Honeywell brand business unlock value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans separate brand and market entry businesses within 2-3 years, but there is no plan for the next 15 months; a demerger process is about 12-15 months and would start once the brand reaches about INR1,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Middle East war on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight on Red Sea routes rose from about $1,500-1,700 to $7,500-8,000 per container; short-term impact is manageable given 45-60 days of partner stock, but a prolonged disruption could halve Middle East brand business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q4 gross and EBITDA margins high?
qa_highlights.answer: Make-in-India surveillance and AI customers, served through smaller vendors, carry higher margins, and the mix is expected to scale as government demand for AI, IoT and data centres grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise to about 20% of turnover and how will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 turnover roughly doubled to INR721 crores from INR393 crores; extended credit for new AI, surveillance and data centre lines is expected to normalise receivables back toward 13-14% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs stay low despite higher short-term debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt excluding MSME supply-chain finance rose only to INR83.72 crores from INR69.53 crores; the rest is about INR171 crores of government TReDS-type MSME payment finance at around 8-9% that started in the last two quarters, so only about 8 months of interest was incurred.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Honeywell licence be renewed and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence expires March 2027; management is very confident of renewal, citing Honeywell's 22-23 year average licences and its split into five companies, with two separated and two more by July-August 2026.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption: Red Sea freight costs and container availability; Middle East brand revenue could fall to about 50% if disruption persists.
Input cost inflation of 30-40% in memory, storage and CPUs, with customers starting to resist price hikes and consumption possibly falling.
Receivables at about 20% of turnover (INR565 crores) versus 13.4% last year; management targets return to 13-14% and inventory is also rising.
Honeywell licence renewal due March 2027; a new licence and trademark terms will need to be confirmed.
Working capital and MSME supply-chain finance (about INR171 crores) rising; watch debt levels and interest costs in coming quarters.
Acquisition plans in surveillance/AI brands and the own-brand launch (Vertual) add execution and funding risk; watch marketing spend of INR10-12 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term growth and brand strategy, but noticeably cautious on the Middle East and input costs, and defensive on receivables, which management attributed to a temporary mix shift. Several answers on the Honeywell split and the brand target were hedged or deferred, and the CFO was introduced mid-call.

growth.why: Management guides consolidated revenue growth of 25-30% a year and brand growth of 50-60% (Honeywell at least 40-50% in FY27), but backing is aspirational: no specific capacity, order or contract numbers were given, and management flagged Middle East disruption and rising memory/CPU costs that could hit sales.
